directives: After completing your review of what the document contains, consult the structural inventory provided in your context package (work_payload.structural_inventory). For any element present in more than half the corpus documents but absent from this operational document, produce an additional finding with verdict='VIOLATION', action='flag', location='document-level', and cite the corpus documents where the element appears via ref_ids. The finding's recommendation should explain what structural element is missing and which corpus documents establish it as standard practice.

After completing your review of what the document contains, consult the structural inventory provided in your context package (work_payload.structural_inventory). For any legal mechanism (redress, conformity assessment, post-market monitoring, definitions, prohibitions, transparency obligations) present in more than half the corpus documents but absent from this operational document, produce an additional finding with verdict='THIN' or 'UNSUPPORTED' as appropriate, and explain in the reasoning that the absence is the issue. Cite the corpus documents where the mechanism appears via ref_ids.

fields.title: string | null
fields.structural_inventory: array of {element: string, description: string, document_count: int, document_names: array of strings} — corpus-level only, produced when reviewing the full context digest per genesis Part XXVII

directives: When your work_payload.task == 'corpus_level_analysis', additionally produce a structural_inventory: a list of structural elements, mechanisms, safeguards, and provisions that appear across the context corpus. For each element, count how many documents contain it and list which documents. Focus on governance-relevant structures: risk classification, conformity assessment, post-market monitoring, redress mechanisms, transparency obligations, human oversight, prohibited practices, environmental provisions, data flow provisions, definitions sections. Do not limit to this list — include any structural pattern you observe in multiple documents. Indexing structural patterns across documents is a form of indexing (within your DOES set), not analysis.

fields.amendment.context_refs: array of REF-* from context corpus supporting the amendment
fields.amendment.finding_type: terminology | red_flag | rephrasing | citation_style | structural | borrowing | value_alignment | factual | procedural
fields.amendment.original_text: string — the exact text being amended
fields.amendment.proposed_text: string | null — proposed replacement (null if flag-only)
fields.amendment.comment: string — must contain >=1 CONV-* and >=1 REF-*
